headline: Kai, the worst market week since 2020 is in the books — a tenth off the Nasdaq, corrections for the S&P and Dow, and a Fed still priced to hike in December.
subline: Bitcoin bounced 5.7% overnight, Iran is moving tankers at the U.S. blockade, and Wednesday packs PCE and GDP into a holiday-shortened week.
asof: Weekend edition · stocks, yield, gold and oil at Friday's close with weekly moves · bitcoin as of ~1 AM ET Sunday · every figure links to its source below

items.title: The tally: Wall Street's worst week since 2020
items.sentence: The S&P 500 lost 8.61%, the Nasdaq 10.02% and the Dow 8.02% for the week, while the 10-year yield eased 24 basis points to 4.91%, per Marketcalls' weekly roundup.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds to $58,944 overnight
items.sentence: It rose 5.68% over 24 hours to $58,944 by early Sunday, per CoinCodex, clawing back part of a week Marketcalls measured at −13.8% with a Saturday-morning low near $56,000.

items.title: December hike odds near 96%, half-point floated
items.sentence: Kalshi, Polymarket and futures pricing put the odds of a December Fed hike near 96% — with an 8.5% chance it is a half point — per Prediction Markets Picks.

items.title: Holiday week ahead: PCE and GDP land Wednesday
items.sentence: Flash PMI opens Monday and consumer confidence follows Tuesday, then October PCE and the second Q3 GDP estimate arrive together Wednesday morning before Thursday's Thanksgiving close, per Financial Juice.

items.title: The rout went global: Nikkei −7.7%
items.sentence: Japan's Nikkei fell 7.70% and Korea's Kospi 7.95% for the week as the U.S. tech selloff spread through Asian markets, per Marketcalls.

items.title: Iran widens Gulf attacks to Kuwait, Bahrain
items.sentence: Iran struck a U.S. air base in Kuwait and targets in Bahrain this week, per The Hill, broadening the conflict beyond its exchanges with U.S. forces in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Iran readies tankers to run the blockade
items.sentence: Even as its missiles hit U.S. bases in Bahrain, Iran's sanctioned tankers are preparing to break the American naval blockade, per Euronews — the weekend's main escalation risk for oil.

items.title: Democrats flipped nine Senate seats this month
items.sentence: The nine midterm pickups are the most by either party in almost 70 years, per AP reporting carried by Cleveland 19, reshaping the Senate Trump will face in January.

items.title: U.S. loses measles elimination status after 26 years
items.sentence: The Pan American Health Organization formally stripped the designation this week amid ongoing outbreaks and falling vaccination rates, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: ANT's first week ends at $88.91
items.sentence: Anthropic closed Friday at $88.91, down 8.5% on 400.5 million shares — still above its $83 offer but well under Thursday's $97.17 finish — and The Motley Fool questions whether 47% sequential revenue growth can carry a $1.5 trillion valuation.

items.title: Nvidia logs seventh straight weekly decline
items.sentence: Shares lost 23% this week — the worst since the 2008 crisis — after Reuters reported SEC staff are examining the company's accounting, per Investing.com, which notes such probes often close without enforcement action.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra edges Gemini 4 Carbon
items.sentence: DataCamp's head-to-head finds OpenAI's November 17 flagship beats Google's Carbon on four of five shared benchmarks, never by more than 3.1 points, while Carbon's lower token price often reverses on reasoning-heavy tasks.

items.title: The AI boom's alarms grow louder
items.sentence: NPR reports that the AI trade's very bad week — Anthropic's debut and Nvidia's slide included — is raising loud alarms about how much of the market now rests on it.
